title: LucidPath — Dedicated Capacity Strategy Workshop
summary: Intro call to align on LucidPath's inference needs: expected steady-state RPS, burst patterns, multi-tenant isolation requirements, and compliance constraints. Explored hosted vs dedicated vs private trade-offs. Agreed Redwood to deliver costed reserved-node options and a small perf run on customer prompt set.
next_steps: Maya to send two reserved-node proposals (baseline + aggressive burst) and pricing sheet by 2026-10-04
Diego to run quick perf microbenchmark on LucidPath sample prompts and share token/sec and P95 numbers by 2026-10-06
LucidPath (Priya) to share sample traffic shape, auth flow, and SSO requirements by 2026-10-05
Schedule technical deep-dive (SE-led) week of 2026-10-11 to walk through VPC/on-prem plan
action_items: Maya Chen: Prepare cost/throughput spreadsheet and two sizing options; Due 2026-10-04
Diego Alvarez: Run sample-prompt microbench and provide perf/latency numbers; Due 2026-10-06
Priya Shah (customer): Share 7-day traffic histogram (RPS by minute) + auth diagram; Due 2026-10-05
Sofia Ritter: Add LucidPath to pilot tracker and send onboarding checklist; Due 2026-10-07
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-01 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez, Sofia Ritter (Redwood); Jordan Lee, Priya Shah, Elliot Moss (LucidPath)
---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood infra team. Quick around the table?
[00:06] Jordan Lee: Jordan from LucidPath, I lead ML infra. We're exploring options to move from our proof-of-concept cluster to a production serving model.
[00:12] Priya Shah: Priya, SRE. I'll own operations and security questions.
[00:16] Elliot Moss: Elliot, CTO, here for strategic fit and timeline.
[00:20] Diego Alvarez: Diego, SE, I'll go deeper on sizing and perf.
[00:24] Sofia Ritter: Sofia, CSM, I'll track the pilot.

[02:00] Maya: Cool. High level, we're trying to understand your traffic profile, what isolation you need, and how bursty you expect things to be so we can show dedicated/reserved options vs hosted. Jordan, can you start with current numbers?
[02:12] Jordan: Sure. Right now in POC we're seeing avg 40 requests/minute, spike up to ~400 for a few hours during marketing pushes. But for production we expect baseline 150 req/min with occasional spikes up to 2k RPS for 10-20 min windows, maybe twice a week.
[02:35] Priya: Right, those spikes are our main concern, and how prewarm or warm-pool works. We can't afford cold-start latency when customer-facing.
[02:44] Diego: Got it. Two thousand RPS short windows, okay, that's a bursty profile. Are those spikes mostly short-lived single-second bursts or sustained minutes?
[02:52] Jordan: Mostly 10-20 minute sustained spikes — not constant. It's more like batch campaign traffic.

[05:10] Diego: For that pattern we usually recommend dedicated reserved nodes plus a hot pool for burst. You can have baseline reserved capacity sized for your steady-state and a warm prewarmed pool that can be used for bursts. We can show baseline sizing and a burst sizing scenario.
[05:22] Elliot: How does billing work for the hot pool? Is it reserved or pay-as-you-go?
[05:28] Maya: Two ways. The reserved nodes are committed monthly (lower unit cost). Hot pool capacity can be either committed or on-demand burst — on-demand has higher unit cost but no long-term commitment. For predictable bursts we recommend reserving a smaller burst tranche.

[07:30] Priya: Isolation — our compliance team wants strict tenant isolation for PII workloads. We need to know if Redwood Dedicated gives hardware-level tenancy or if it's logical isolation.
[07:41] Diego: Redwood Dedicated offers node-level isolation. We can provision dedicated GPU pools per account or per tenant, depending on the contract. For strict PII we can do single-tenant pools and private control plane in a VPC or on-prem combo.
[07:58] Jordan: When you say "private control plane" is that the Redwood Private product? We're evaluating hosted, dedicated, and private.
[08:05] Maya: Yes. Hosted is quickest to get started; Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with isolation and predictable throughput; Private gives you the control plane in your VPC or on-prem for the strictest compliance. Often customers start Dedicated and move to Private for full air-gapped needs.

[10:12] Elliot: Timeline — we want production by end of Q1 2027. Is that reasonable? Any long lead times for reserved GPU procurement?
[10:20] Diego: From a provisioning standpoint, we can usually spin up dedicated pools in our cloud regions within a few weeks after contract. If you require specific on-prem hardware, that adds procurement and integration time.
[10:30] Maya: We'd align contract milestones to your timeline. For Q1 rollout let's plan a pilot on Dedicated in November/December and expand in Jan-Feb.

[12:44] Jordan: Security — SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS integration are must-haves. Can Redwood integrate with our Azure AD and our KMS HSM?
[12:52] Diego: Yes we support SAML/SSO, RBAC, API keys, and KMS integrations for key material. Audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM. For Private deployments we can integrate with your HSM.
[13:05] Priya: How are logs retained and where? We need audit logs for 12 months and export to our Splunk.
[13:12] Maya: We can keep logs in our control plane for X days by default and offer extended retention as an add-on. We'll provide an export connector to Splunk — I'll attach the docs.

[15:00] Elliot: Any SOC 2 / ISO certifications?
[15:04] Sofia: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and pursuing ISO27001 — we can share the report under NDA.

[17:30] Diego: Let's talk perf. Jordan, do you have sample prompts?
[17:36] Jordan: Yes we can share a small set — a mix of long-context summarization prompts and short classification calls. Latency SLO is P95 < 350ms for short prompts.
[17:46] Diego: For P95 under 350ms we need to size for low-latency instance types and tune batching. Also caching helps for prefix patterns. Note: sometimes model names in our perf deck got garbled in transcripts — we run real kernels optimized for attention.
[18:10] Jordan: Quick question — quantization, will that change accuracy? We can't degrade model quality for some workloads.
[18:18] Diego: Quantization can affect quality depending on model and task. We suggest testing the quantized variant as part of the pilot; Redwood Optimize can recommend quant profiles that balance accuracy and cost. We'll run evals on your prompts.

[20:54] Priya: Networking — are we forced through public internet with Dedicated? We need traffic to stay within our VPC for security.
[21:01] Maya: No, Dedicated supports private networking (VPC peering or PrivateLink equivalents). For Private deployments we can also provide a customer-managed control plane inside your VPC.
[21:10] Priya: Great. And what about egress costs?
[21:14] Diego: Egress is billed by the cloud provider normally; we can discuss architecture to minimize cross-region traffic. We'll show region placement and cost implications in the proposal.

[23:30] Jordan: On the operational side, how do rollouts work? We want canary plus automatic fallback to smaller models if latency spikes.
[23:38] Diego: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B, and automated fallback policies that can route to cheaper model variants when SLOs breach. You can pin versions and configure fallback chains.

[25:45] Elliot: Are there limits on model variants we can host? We need LLMs that are fine-tuned internal models.
[25:52] Diego: You can bring your own models; we support standard model formats. For private deployment we'll work through the onboarding process to load them securely and provide quantization/optimization as needed.

[28:00] Jordan: Pricing — ballpark numbers for reserved capacity and burst?
[28:06] Maya: We'll share two options: conservative baseline sized for steady-state and a second option with reserved burst tranche. Baseline gives you lower per-token and per-inference cost. Burst will be higher but reduces cold-start risk. We'll include amortized prewarm cost.

[30:12] Priya: SLA — we need 99.9% uptime and clear latency SLAs. Is that part of Dedicated?
[30:18] Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; for enterprise contracts we can include contractual SLAs and support SLAs.

[33:00] Jordan: One more technical — KV cache / prefix caching. Our prompts often reuse prior context; can that be cached across requests to reduce compute?
[33:09] Diego: Yes, Redwood supports KV/prefix caching and shared session caches to reduce redundant compute. That helps a lot for multi-turn workloads.

[35:50] Priya: Data residency — some customers require EU-only processing. Can you guarantee regional processing?
[35:58] Diego: Yes, we can pin model serving and control plane to regions; Private lets you keep control plane in-region as well.

[38:12] Elliot: Any migration risks? We're concerned about changing inference infra mid-quarter.
[38:19] Sofia: We usually recommend a phased pilot: shadow traffic first, then canary, then cutover. We'll provide runbooks and rollback.

[40:40] Jordan: On the perf microbench — what's realistic for us to expect? For our sample prompts, if Diego runs a bench, what metrics will you return?
[40:49] Diego: I'll return tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, GPU utilization, and estimated cost per 1M tokens under both reserved and on-demand. We'll show prewarm ramp times.

[43:00] Priya: Compliance docs — please share SOC2 report and the KMS integration doc.
[43:06] Maya: I'll share SOC2 under NDA; also the KMS/HSM integration guide and the audit log export doc.

[45:15] Elliot: Decision criteria — what do you need from us to make your next recommendation internally?
[45:22] Jordan: We'll need clear TCO for baseline vs aggressive burst, timeline, and details on isolation so security can sign off.

[47:30] Maya: Recap: Redwood actions — pricing + two sizing proposals, perf microbench, security docs. LucidPath actions — traffic histogram and auth/SAML requirements. Schedule SE deep-dive after docs.

[48:05] Priya: Sounds good. One minor thing — we use Azure primarily, just FYI, and we have a custom HSM.
[48:12] Diego: Noted. For Azure we'll check region availability and HSM integration specifics.

[50:00] Jordan: Quick aside — we evaluated some vendor who had weird prewarm behavior and it taxed our GPU; any guardrails?
[50:08] Diego: We have autoscale guardrails, prewarm quotas, and burst throttles to prevent over-allocation. We'll include recommended autoscale policies in the proposal.

[51:20] Maya: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the proposal and schedule the deep dive.
[51:28] Elliot: Thanks.
[51:30] Meeting end.
